clinician.final_diagnosis: B-ALL (B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia) associated with t(1;4)(p21;p15) chromosomal abnormality
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 4-year-old Moroccan girl presented with a 20-day history of pharyngitis, fever, asthenia, and paleness. Physical examination revealed an abscess fistulated in the left labia majora (E001). Complete blood count showed severe anemia (Hb 6.0 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (PLT 41,000/mm³), and normal WBC (8,100/mm³) with low neutrophils (570/mm³) (E003), consistent with bone marrow infiltration. Bone marrow aspiration demonstrated 97% blast cells with heterogeneous size, reduced cytoplasm, condensed chromatin, and basophilic appearance without granulations (E004), diagnostic of acute leukemia. Flow cytometry on bone marrow showed aberrant expression of CD13, a myeloid marker (E005). Karyotype analysis on 20 mitoses revealed a translocation between the short arm of chromosome 1 and the short arm of chromosome 4 in 10 mitoses: 46,XX,t(1;4)(p21;p15)[10]/46,XX[10] (E006). Complementary FISH analysis excluded MLL gene rearrangement or deletion in all 200 mitoses examined (E007), ruling out MLL-rearranged leukemia. The constellation of morphologic findings (97% blasts), cytogenetic evidence (t(1;4) translocation), and immunophenotypic findings (CD13 aberrant expression) in the context of acute leukemia presentation establishes the diagnosis of B-ALL with t(1;4).

Flow cytometry on bone marrow showed aberrant expression of CD13, a myeloid marker (E005). Karyotype analysis on 20 mitoses revealed a translocation between the short arm of chromosome 1 and the short arm of chromosome 4 in 10 mitoses: 46,XX,t(1;4)(p21;p15)[10]/46,XX[10] (E006). Complementary FISH analysis excluded MLL gene rearrangement or deletion in all 200 mitoses examined (E007), ruling out MLL-rearranged leukemia. The constellation of morphologic findings (97% blasts), cytogenetic evidence (t(1;4) translocation), and immunophenotypic findings (CD13 aberrant expression) in the context of acute leukemia presentation establishes the diagnosis of B-ALL with t(1;4).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: 4-year-old Moroccan girl with 20-day history of pharyngitis, fever, asthenia, and paleness
Physical examination finding of abscess fistulated in left labia majora
Severe anemia (Hb 6.0 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (PLT 41,000/mm³), and normal WBC with low neutrophils (570/mm³) indicating bone marrow infiltration
Bone marrow aspiration showing 97% blast cells with morphology consistent with acute leukemia (heterogeneous size, reduced cytoplasm, condensed chromatin, basophilic, no granulations)
Flow cytometry demonstrating aberrant CD13 expression (myeloid marker) on blasts
Karyotype analysis confirming t(1;4)(p21;p15) translocation in 10 of 20 mitoses: 46,XX,t(1;4)(p21;p15)[10]/46,XX[10]
FISH analysis excluding MLL gene rearrangement or deletion in all 200 mitoses examined

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: FISH analysis showed absence of MLL gene rearrangement or deletion in all 200 mitoses (E007)
While CD13 (myeloid marker) was aberrantly expressed, the morphologic findings and cytogenetic abnormality t(1;4) are consistent with B-ALL rather than de novo AML
Bone marrow aspiration revealed 97% blast cells diagnostic of acute leukemia, not reactive changes (E004)

remaining_uncertainties: Complete immunophenotyping panel with explicit B-cell marker status (CD19, CD20, CD10, CD34, TdT) was not fully documented in available records; only aberrant CD13 expression was reported
Cytochemical staining results (MPO, PAS, Sudan black) were not documented
Systemic examination findings regarding lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly were not reported
Treatment regimen, clinical course, and treatment response were not documented in available records
The molecular identity of the fusion gene(s) resulting from t(1;4)(p21;p15) was not explicitly stated in available records

evaluation.known_final_diagnosis: We present a case of a 4-year-old Moroccan girl who was diagnosed with B-ALL associated with a t(1;4) chromosomal abnormality in 2016.
